3-11.caveats: Only one laboratory study exists, and its participants were healthy young adults. If you can’t fall asleep, there’s no need to force it; there’s no research showing any benefit from simply lying down with eyes closed for 10 minutes. Naps longer than an hour have been linked to higher mortality and increased risk of coronary heart disease — see Section 2, Item 38 (keep naps under 30 minutes).

3-18.benefit: This meta-analysis combined data from 218 randomized controlled trials involving 14,170 participants; the control group performed other activities. Compared with them, walking or running lowered depression scores by g = -0.62 (95% CI -0.80 to -0.45). Yoga produced g = -0.55 and strength training g = -0.49; higher intensity further improved outcomes. Pooled data from multiple light‑therapy studies showed an effect size of 0.84 (0.60–1.08) for seasonal depression and 0.53 (0.18–0.89) for non‑seasonal cases. Another analysis aggregated individual‑patient data from various studies on internet‑based cognitive‑behavioral therapy; both self‑guided and therapist‑supervised programs outperformed controls, with therapist guidance yielding better results for moderate‑to‑severe depression (PHQ‑9 score >9). The 14416 (Tele-MANAS) hotline provides nationwide psychological support round the clock, every day.

3-19.benefit: Switching to this approach means moving from “pleading, getting angry, and reiterating your grievances” to “handling paperwork, tracking deadlines, and appealing via official routes.” The time saved comes from eliminating endless back-and-forth discussions and mental re-processing. This is a one-time mindset shift rather than a daily time-saving trick. The appeal routes are the concrete checkpoints: each one is written into the rules and produces a document you can point to, rather than being decided at the counter. Take the police: under section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 the officer in charge must register a first information report when you report a cognisable offence, and give you a copy free of cost; if the station refuses, section 175 lets you complain to the Superintendent of Police and then to the magistrate. What you get is a documented route with a dated record at each step.
3-19.caveats: Grade C is assigned because there is no scholarly source supporting the premise that “many people treat front-desk staff as archetypes rather than ordinary workers.” The only evidence lies in the rules themselves: paperwork, acknowledgement and appeal mechanisms are explicitly codified. The police route summarised here is the one in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, set out in Chapter 8, Rule 39: a right to have a cognisable offence registered and a copy given free of cost, and a route to the Superintendent of Police and then the magistrate. It does not fix a schedule for the investigation, so treat any deadline you are quoted at a counter as something to confirm in the statute rather than assume. This entry does not promise to “guarantee success” by following the rules, nor does it address “unfriendly attitudes” on the part of officials. It merely shifts expectations and the initial course of action. The same logic applies to bank tellers and government service windows: their actions are documented, subject to review, and accountable for errors. Therefore, the proper steps are to keep receipts, request written confirmations, and file complaints through official channels — rather than speculating about whether someone might “take advantage” of you. Legitimate priorities are laid out in law; for example, emergency care is allocated based on medical severity, not on first-come-first-served order (see Chapter 24, Rule 8 on triage). If you wish to thank a doctor who helped you, send a thank-you letter or leave a satisfaction rating as described in Chapter 24, Rule 11. Offering gifts to law-enforcement personnel to “get better service” constitutes bribery, a crime with severe statutory penalties (see Chapter 8, Rule 40). Any obvious discrimination should be reported and monitored, not imitated as an unwritten norm.

3-25.cost: A strip of over-the-counter ibuprofen costs a few tens of rupees, taken only during symptomatic days. If clinical evaluation is required, an outpatient consultation and pelvic ultrasonography take half a day and the usual consultation fee.

3-27.cost: Involves consultation at a sleep center, pulmonology, or ENT clinic. Diagnostic polysomnography (overnight sleep study) is conducted in-hospital or via home sleep apnea testing devices. For moderate-to-severe disease requiring continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), buying a CPAP machine is a large out-of-pocket purchase — tens of thousands of rupees, before the mask and the filters. The primary hurdle is behavioral persistence: wearing a nasal or oronasal mask nightly takes weeks to adapt, and many patients discontinue use after a few hours per night.
